pharm: Inhibits transmembrane calcium influx through L-type voltage-gated channels in vascular smooth muscle and cardiac muscle, causing arterial vasodilation.
quick: Used when benefit outweighs risk (e.g., severe hypertension/tocolysis)
Excreted in milk; generally considered compatible

Blood pressure, heart rate, peripheral edema
summary: Nifedipine is a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker used to manage hypertension and vasospastic (Prinzmetal) and chronic stable angina. Extended-release formulations are preferred because immediate-release nifedipine can cause reflex tachycardia and abrupt hypotension. It produces potent arterial vasodilation with little effect on cardiac conduction. Dose-related peripheral edema, flushing, and headache are common.

dosage.d: Initial 30-60 mg once daily; titrate over 7-14 days
dosage.n: Swallow whole; do not exceed 120 mg/day

dosage.d: Initial 30-60 mg once daily; titrate as needed
30-60 mg once daily, titrated to response
Use lower doses and titrate cautiously

admin: Swallow the extended-release tablet whole; do not bite, divide, chew, or crush
Avoid grapefruit juice for the duration of therapy
Titrate over a 7-14 day period while monitoring blood pressure
Do not discontinue abruptly; taper to avoid rebound
An empty tablet shell (ghost tablet) in the stool with osmotic formulations is harmless
moa: Nifedipine inhibits calcium ion influx through L-type voltage-dependent calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle and myocardium. The predominant effect is relaxation of arterial smooth muscle, which dilates peripheral and coronary arteries, lowering systemic vascular resistance and blood pressure and relieving coronary vasospasm. This reduces myocardial oxygen demand and improves oxygen delivery in angina.

relative: Concomitant beta-blocker with high-dose fentanyl anesthesia (severe hypotension)
Unstable angina or acute MI (immediate-release form may worsen ischemia)
monitor: Signs of worsening angina at initiation/titration

preg: Animal studies showed teratogenicity and embryotoxicity at high doses. Nifedipine is used in pregnancy when clearly needed (e.g., severe hypertension, off-label tocolysis) under specialist guidance; weigh benefit against risk.
lact: Nifedipine is excreted in breast milk in small amounts and is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding; observe the infant.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is required for renal impairment; titrate to clinical response.
hepatic: Nifedipine is extensively metabolized by the liver (CYP3A4); reduce the dose and titrate cautiously in hepatic impairment because clearance is decreased and exposure increased.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir) - markedly increase nifedipine levels and hypotension
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin) - reduce nifedipine efficacy (avoid)
High-dose fentanyl anesthesia with concomitant beta-blocker - severe hypotension
moderate: Beta-blockers (additive hypotension; usually well tolerated but monitor)
interactions.food: Avoid grapefruit juice, which inhibits CYP3A4 and increases nifedipine levels; take the tablet whole.
interactions.alcohol: May enhance the hypotensive and vasodilatory effects.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause a positive direct Coombs test and rarely false elevations of certain enzymes; no routine assay interference of clinical significance.

monitoring: Liver function if symptoms suggest hepatic injury
counsel: Swallow the tablet whole; never crush or chew the extended-release form
You may notice the empty tablet shell in your stool - this is normal for some long-acting forms
Swelling of the ankles, headache, or flushing may occur and often eases with time
Do not stop the medicine suddenly; rise slowly to avoid dizziness
pk: Terminal ~2 hours (immediate-release); apparent longer with ER delivery
Store at 20-25 C; protect from light and moisture
pearls: Prefer extended-release; immediate-release/sublingual nifedipine can cause dangerous reflex tachycardia and is not for hypertensive emergencies
Peripheral edema is dose-related and not due to fluid overload - does not respond well to diuretics
Avoid grapefruit juice (CYP3A4 inhibition raises levels)
Potent arteriolar dilator with minimal effect on AV conduction (unlike verapamil/diltiazem)
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the normal schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Overdose causes marked hypotension, bradycardia or reflex tachycardia, and conduction disturbances. Treat with supportive care, IV fluids and vasopressors, calcium salts, and high-dose insulin-euglycemia therapy in severe cases. Nifedipine is highly protein-bound and not effectively dialyzable.
